translationRepairs: He captured Tian Guang, the former king of Qi; Tian Guang, his chancellor; Xu Zhang, acting chancellor in charge of the defense; and Tian Ji, the former Jiaodong general.
He captured Tian Guang, the chancellor of the former King of Qi Tian Guang; Xu Zhang, the defending chancellor; and Tian Ji, the former Jiaodong general of Qi.
得故齊王田廣相田光 names captives starting with chancellor 田光 of former Qi king 田廣, not the king himself; the proposed list restores that parse and keeps 守相許章 and 故齊膠東將軍田既.
Among his prisoners were the former King of Qi, Tian Guang, Chancellor Tian Guang, the defending chancellor Xu Zhang, and the former Jiaodong general Tian Ji.
He obtained the former King of Qi Tian Guang's chancellor Tian Guang, his defending chancellor Xu Zhang, and the former Jiaodong general of Qi Tian Ji.
The literal likewise misreads 故齊王田廣相田光 as capturing both king and chancellor; 得 takes 相田光 (and then 守相許章, 將軍田既) as the objects obtained.
His fief income was Pingyang with 16,630 households, titled Marquis of Pingyang, removing his previous fief income.
His fief income was Pingyang with 10,630 households, titled Marquis of Pingyang, removing his previous fief income.
食邑平陽萬六百三十戶 is 10,630 households (萬 + 六百三十), not 16,630; the proposed numeral matches the Chinese and the idiomatic reading.
His son Dai succeeded as marquis.
His son Shi succeeded as marquis.
子時代侯 parallels 子奇代侯: 時 is the personal name Shi and 代侯 means succeeded as marquis, so Dai is a false name from misreading 代.
Dai married Princess Pingyang, fathering son Xiang.
Shi married Princess Pingyang, fathering son Xiang.
時尚平陽公主 continues the subject 時 (Shi) from the prior sentence; Dai is not in the Chinese.
Dai fell ill and returned to his state.
Shi fell ill and returned to his state.
時病癘，歸國 likewise has 時 as Shi; replacing Dai with Shi corrects the same misread personal name.
Xiang married Princess Chang Wei, fathering son Zong.
Xiang married the Elder Princess of Wei, fathering son Zong.
衛長公主 is the Elder Princess of Wei (衛 + 長公主), not a personal name Chang Wei; the proposed title matches the Chinese and the idiomatic rendering.
